chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mihran, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second wrote to a man: 'You mentioned your bereavement with your son Ali, and mentioned that he was the most beloved of your children to you, and likewise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, only takes from the parent and others the purest of what is with his family to magnify through it the reward of the bereaved by the bereavement. So may Allah magnify your reward, and make your consolation good, and strengthen your heart, indeed He is Powerful, and may Allah hasten the successor to you, and I hope that Allah has done so, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.'
ai.seo_question: What is the theological reason for Allah taking the most beloved child according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This epistle from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes the theological principle that Allah selects the most virtuous ('azka') members of a family for death to maximize the reward of the bereaved, a concept deeply rooted in Shia understanding of divine wisdom. The letter not only offers consolation but also links personal loss to the broader eschatological hope of the reappearance of the Imam, encouraging the father to remain steadfast. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on viewing trials as opportunities for spiritual elevation and connection to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mihran who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup> wrote to a man: ‘You mentioned your difficulties (bereavement) with your son Ali, and mentioned that he was the most beloved of your children to you, and like that does Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Take from the parent and other the most pure of the one in the presence of the family in order to Magnify the Recompense of the bereavement by it, by the bereavement. Therefore, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Magnify your Recompense, and Grant the best of the comforts, and attachment upon your heart, and may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Hasten upon you with the successor, and I<sup>asws</sup> am hoping that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would have done so, Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Exalted, Willing’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mehran who has said the following: “

Abu Ja’far, the second, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, wrote to a man, T was informed of your suffering from the death of your son, Ali. I was also informed that he was the most beloved among your sons to you. It so happens that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, takes away from a father or other people the most beloved to his people so as to increase their reward for their suffering. May Allah increase your reward, grant you patience and strengthen your heart; He is Most powerful. May Allah very soon grant you one to replace him and I hope that Allah has already made it happen.’”
